counterfactual_missing_items: A postpacing interval within 20 ms when pacing at the mitral isthmus scar
Typical atrial flutter with a sawtooth pattern
decisive_items: an epicardial pathway bypassing the scar
recordings showed activation within the vein of Marshall that matched the tachycardia cycle length
postpacing interval more than 20 ms longer than the cycle length when pacing adjacent to the mitral isthmus scar
response.rationale: R2 is the only candidate that directly identifies the epicardial bypass via the vein of Marshall, which is the key finding. R5 is a broader scar-related category but lacks the specific mechanism. R1 is contradicted by the entrainment at the mitral isthmus showing a longer postpacing interval. R4 is incorrect as the rhythm is atrial tachycardia, not fibrillation.

rejected.why: The rhythm is atrial tachycardia with a regular cycle length and P waves, not atrial fibrillation.
While scar-related, the specific epicardial bypass via the vein of Marshall is more specific and directly supported.
The entrainment at the mitral isthmus shows a postpacing interval >20 ms longer, indicating the scar is not in the circuit, ruling out mitral isthmus-dependent flutter.
